# Genuine registry 0.33 schema witness

These immutable, MIT-licensed synthetic files were generated on November 10, 2026 by an isolated consumer of the actual published 0.33.0 core, gallery, renderer and PPTX packages. `receipt.json` records their registry integrity, release gitHead, isolated installed paths, options and source validation. `registry033.pptx` is 113,310 bytes with SHA-256 `80c53d0482cfd385f6745d4c7af6143d212d0b053bbb8e9a21236297f18be4da`. No current workspace package or unpublished prototype generated it.

`source.opf.json` retains the old `left` / `right`, run `lang` and overloaded anchor dimensions exactly as exported. `registry033-import.opf.json` is the actual 0.33 importer result, including its existing canonicalization. Never mechanically migrate or regenerate these historical sources to make a test pass. The new regression constructs its expected current document by changing only the explicitly asserted structural fields; authored text, code, extension keys/values and scalar datasets remain exact.

The witness contains three slides: two legacy pixel anchors (160 and the 1.01 boundary), plain text/code literals, a rich table with French language and a physical left border, and a chart referencing a scalar dataset whose category is the same path-like literal. The root coordinator generated it; neither this archive nor its test is an actual PowerPoint Save/reopen/edit observation. Test-only ZIP/XML mutations simulate current native text and cache changes and retain the original archive.

For an independent replay, copy `generate.mjs`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `registry-identities.json` into a new directory outside every workspace, install with pinned pnpm 10.33.2 under Node 24, and run `node generate.mjs`. The generator refuses non-isolated package paths and checks lock integrities. It uses registered `[gallery]` catalogs and the eight exact pinned permissive font peers; no font binary is stored in this fixture. The first invalid-catalog call and missing-font-peer failures are retained literally in the two attempt logs. Replay creates its own `output/`; it must not overwrite these fixtures.
